components.rationale: RB-028 / Rev 1.5 §18. The broker was constructed in `create_app` and called by nothing: `GET /downloads` read the table directly and no route ever wrote a row. A correct component nothing invokes is the shape this programme keeps finding, so the two authorities that touch a download now have routes — Hermes reports what the host saw, the owner deletes and is told what they may do with each file. The report surface accepts no state name, so §18.2's pipeline decides where a file stops rather than the caller.

components.rationale: RB-046 / Rev 1.5 §13.2. `agent.py` says nothing about transport and `server.py` starts no listener, which left two implementations of the same protocol with nothing between them to disagree with. The encoding carries references — task, lease, generation — and refuses a message that names its own caller, scope or budget, so the authority check cannot be answered by the thing it checks. Framing lives here too, for the same reason: where one message ends is the other thing two implementations can disagree about while both look right, and a test asserts no encoded message can contain the delimiter rather than assuming the encoder will keep escaping control characters.

RB-046 / Rev 1.5 §§13, 28. `browser.interactive.session` is declared EXTERNAL_RUNTIME against the `browser_stream_host` probe, so a Mission cannot record that it used a remote browser until a canary has measured one. This is the only thing in the repository that writes that evidence, and it needs a host address with no offline mode.

components.production_caller: an operator, against a provisioned host

components.rationale: RB-043 / Rev 1.5 §§22.2, 22.3 and ADR-RB-007. What Hermes is handed when it drives the owner's browser, and what is destroyed when the owner takes it back. §22.3 names the insufficient implementation directly — a UI-only "Take over" button without server-side invalidation — and the half that was missing was the queued actions: the generation already moved, and an action already accepted was still waiting to run.

components.rationale: RB-047 / Rev 1.5 §28.1. Four measurements neither the Gateway nor the Stream Host can take: the Gateway is not in the media path by design and the host can say what it sent, not what arrived. `browser_last_frame_age_ms` is the number behind a frozen picture, which from the owner's side is indistinguishable from a slow page. Two of the four had reached the Gateway's catalogue beside a dict the device-telemetry contract test did not read, so nothing checked that a phone could post them. `DecoderStats` sits beside it for the same reason: a stats report carries an `inbound-rtp` entry per media kind, and reading the first one reports the audio decoder's drops as the picture's. Which entry to read is a decision, so it is pure and executed here; the JNI call that fetches the report is not.
components.producer: com.dial.van.telemetry.BrowserStreamTelemetry and DecoderStats, fed from the WebRTC video sink and from a stats poll on the session heartbeat

components.rationale: RB-089/090/091 / Rev 1.5 §12. A Samsung pop-up window dragged by its corner produces a resize callback per frame; the difference between a browser that survives that and one that renegotiates a remote Chromium sixty times a second is a debounce, a cadence and an atomic swap. All three are arithmetic over window bounds, so all three are executed here rather than reasoned about. Writing the tests found two defects in this file: a `Long.MIN_VALUE` sentinel that overflowed the cadence subtraction so the first candidate of a session was never sent, and a missing baseline that made a one-pixel inset rounding a material resize.
components.owner_facing_projection: The picture following the window while the remote browser catches up

components.rationale: RB-026 / §17.2. components.rationale: RB-027 / §§17.1, 17.6. A reducer over the four events §17.1 names: the phone holds a projection of Chromium's targets and never invents one. §17.6's Back order is here because its last clause is a prohibition — Back must not close the browser while the page has history.

components.rationale: RB-095–099 / §5.8, §17.5, ADR-RB-023. An external link opens in the public profile, fixed rather than parameterised, because a link from a messaging app opening in the browser holding the owner's logged-in cookies is the whole of the attack.
